jobs.title: Product Engineer (all levels)
jobs.description:
👋 Hi, I’m Sina, CTO at Nous. 

I’ve spent my entire career in startups, starting my first company when I was a teenager, and navigated many 0→1 journeys (including starting the largest social network of its time in my home country).

The common thread that led me here is finding complexity that wastes people’s time or money, then solving for making them disappear. And that’s exactly what Nous aims to do.

If this problem space resonates, please read on. 

PS: I’ve actually written this page with my hands; this is not AI-written content!

About Nous

Roughly 90% of UK households are overpaying on their bills. Nous is an agent to absorb complexity out of households, saving them money and time. Our mission is to make people’s lives simpler and fairer, starting with the 30 million households here in the UK, and soon far beyond.

Nous is growing fast, and it’s working. 20x YoY growth makes us one of the fastest scaling startups in the UK. And NPS of +70 (higher than Apple) shows that our users love it.

We’ve just launched two novel new products (on top of our current service lines). Insurance: we’re the first to get the regulatory approval and build the tech to actually do the full insurance discovery and purchase journey as an agent for the user (not just give them a link to the best deal). Subscription management: lots of companies use open banking to draw pretty graphs - we’re the first to use it to actively save people money starting by cancelling unwanted subscriptions for them.

It would be easy to look at this and think we’ve got it all figured out.

But we’ve only scratched the surface; our ambitions are SO much higher. We started with bills because ‘change begins at home’ - it’s a naturally low-interest, messy area of our lives which most of us don’t want to think about. Similar to how Amazon started with books as their first category to go after.

‘Talk is cheap. Action is what really matters’. What we’re building is an agent to take some of the load of life, make good decisions and act for us in areas we can’t or don’t want to act on our own. For an agent, advice is cheap. Action is the product. And action means solving problems in the messy real world.

A note on product

There’s ‘product’ as in the web application that guides our users through the complex world of bills and household admin. It acts as their interface to our management service, as well as all the behind the scenes capabilities needed to orchestrate and deliver that service - actually saving our users money and time. Try it here: app.nous.co/signup (it’s free!)

Then there’s ‘product’ as experienced by our users - which is a service which makes life simple and fair. To deliver this we’ve built a set of powerful capabilities that let us run and improve the service efficiently at scale: agentic communication, multimodal data extraction, orchestration for long-running operational processes, recommendations, our own agentic harness, and more. We compose these into executable workflows that deliver real outcomes for members, like switching someone to a better energy deal without the hassle.

Today, we help manage six areas of household spending: Energy, Mobile, Broadband, Mortgage, Personal finances (e.g., managing subscriptions), and Insurance. But we’re just getting started. Behind the scenes, we’ve built the technology (we call it Blueprints) that acts as rails for us to quickly expand on the breadth and depth of our service lines.

The role

We need your help building a world-class product that will be used regularly by millions of people; which means figuring out, together, what it really takes to absorb household complexity.

As a product engineer, we'll empower you with context to enable fast iterations, end-to-end ownership and lots of agency. You’ll be a hands-on technical leader on some of the highest-leverage areas of our codebase, from building out agentic capabilities to scaling our service logic.

Some examples of the types of problems you'll solve:

  • Anton led and shipped an entire product line around open banking and subscription management three months after joining. Yes, he had support from legal, design, commercial and his team (we even became FCA registered). But one product engineer still took it from idea to a best-in-class product in the category.

  • Ed led the our latest Blueprint architecture, which now powers every service line. Changes to complex, long-running workflows that once took weeks can now sometimes take minutes. All safely, reliably and with full type safety.

  • Tim led and shipped our car insurance product line, in less than 3 months. We built a journey where an agent performs the discovery and purchase journeys - something that's not been done before and needed problem solving at the intersection of engineering, product and regulatory.

  • As a team, we built our own agentic harness (we call it super-engineer); it’s enabled us to build faster, investigate complex cross-system issues effectively; and it self-improves.

There are also so many interesting problems we are in the infancy of solving. Just as an example - user’s trust us with their Open Banking data - but it’s just lists of transactions. How can we use that stream of information and combine it with all the other data we have, to reduce friction from their lives?

Every week, we’re building tools for ourselves and evolving how we work, to make ourselves more effective. I strongly believe in the value of compounding gains, and much of our focus goes into investing in what results in exponential growth.


Although our stack is constantly evolving (and you can help shape that), here’s a current snapshot:

  • Full-stack TypeScript, React, Postgres, and Temporal for long-running orchestration.

  • Infra: AWS, Terraform, strong observability via Sentry and Datadog (full-stack, not just logs).

  • Data: we lean heavily on Snowflake, Omni, dbt, Fivetran, Amplitude and Segment — and we’ve even built some of our own tooling to understand how well we’re helping our members.

  • And we use Github, Linear, Graphite, and Blacksmith every day. We choose the best tool for the job, and don’t obsess around specific technologies.

  • We also heavily rely on our wide range of agentic and tooling harness that we build and iterate on across the team. They’re part of the “secret” behind how we move fast, reliably.

You’ll report directly to the CTO (and we’ll work closely), so will be in the room for key architectural and product decisions. We’re deliberately light on layers of management: exceptional individual contributors shape direction by solving hard problems.


We organise around small product squads (around 5–7 people) with a single shared objective; and ship and learn fast.

You'll build in two modes

This is the bit that makes the role different, so it's worth being clear about.

Sometimes you build the product directly. That might mean a new product line, a core product improvement; or an exciting new idea to experiment on the product. You're usually working with one or two others, moving fast from a rough plan and jumping on problems as they surface.

Sometimes you build the multiplier. The safe surfaces and shared tooling that let a non-engineer ship without breaking things. Think the internal equivalent of what Lovable did for "anyone can put a website live", but for our problems: bills, switching, household admin at scale.

Both are hard engineering work. And the two feed each other: the better the multiplier you build, the more the genuinely deep problems are the ones left for you. Leverage for the ops team is leverage for you.

What we look for

You don't need to tick every box. If you read these and feel a mix of "this is me" and "this would stretch me", you're probably right for it.

  • You own problems end to end. You're happiest going from fuzzy pain to shipped fix to the numbers that show it worked. You instinctively ask "what's the smallest thing we can ship to learn?" instead of waiting for a perfect spec.

  • You think like a PM as much as an engineer. You care about the problem, the user, flow, UX, and even copy as much as correctness, because you've seen a small wording change flip confusion into action.

  • You're a pragmatic builder. Clean, practical code others can extend. You know when to abstract and when to keep it brutally simple to go fast. You'll happily delete your own code when reality disagrees with it.

  • You build leverage for other people. You explain complex things simply, you pair on gnarly problems, and you leave things clearer than you found them. You see a good tool that unblocks a teammate as real work, not a distraction from it.

  • You're here for the problem. Fairness, money and complexity, made manageable for people who don't have time to fight the system themselves. You'd rather work hard on something that genuinely helps.

We hire across all levels (mid-senior, to staff+), with a minimum 2 years of professional experience. The size and independence of your initial scope will reflect your experience, but the shape of the role is the same: you own outcomes. For earlier-career candidates, our assessment is primarily on your growth trajectory.

This probably isn't for you if…

  • You want a clear remit handed down before you can move. Here you get lots of context and invested colleagues, not a manager translating the work into tickets for you.

  • You believe nothing should ship unless it routes through a gate you personally control. The control we care about is structural: guardrails in the tools, not who's allowed to type. If that sounds too loose, we'll probably frustrate each other.

  • You want to specialise narrowly and stay in one layer. The role is broad by design.

What to expect

As CTO, and the person hiring for this role, you can hold me to these promises:

  • You’ll never be bored. You’ll continuously have difficult and interesting challenges to solve

  • The rest of the team and I will empower you with context, and will involve you as a co-founder

  • You’ll be learning every day, solve new challenges, and sometimes find yourself running while simultaneously learning how to run

  • You’ll have the space and support to grow your AI engineering skills, whether through harness engineering, trying new approaches, or even going as far as inventing new ways of solving problems. We’re building at the edge of what is possible, and we are conscious that there’s trial and error and first principles thinking involved in figuring it out

  • You’ll work closely with a caring and highly intelligent team. It’s ok, stalk us on Linkedin and check for yourself

  • 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

  • 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

  • ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

  • 💰 A generous cash referral bonus if you introduce us to someone who joins the team

That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. jobs.description:
🍊Our mission

Great science regularly stalls in the clinic, not because the science is wrong, but because the company behind it lacks the capital, infrastructure, or focus to take it all the way through. Today’s clinical-stage biopharma model is broken, and as a result promising treatments never reach patients.

Our mission is to fix this: we’re building the next generation of biopharma by in-licensing clinical-stage therapeutic assets and developing them through Lindus Health’s integrated, technology-first clinical trial infrastructure. We’re a new initiative, but we’re building on a proven foundation - the same infrastructure that has delivered 82% of Lindus Health’s sponsor trials on or ahead of timeline, across 40+ completed trials across the US and Europe.

We’re in-licensing 5-7 clinical-stage, typically Phase-2-ready assets, funded directly from Lindus Health’s balance sheet. We’re targeting deal close on our first assets through 2026, with first trials launching in H1 2027.

🍊 About the role

As Lindus Therapeutics builds out its portfolio through in-licensing, the Director of Biostatistics owns statistical strategy across that portfolio and stays hands-on, personally leading the statistics on live programmes from protocol through clinical study report. It's a genuine coach-player role - as much applied biostatistician as director.

This seat carries real weight: the statistical rigour of an incoming asset's data package shapes deal terms and development risk, and it's Lindus Therapeutics' primary statistical voice with regulators. You'll work closely with clinical, medical, data architecture, and business development colleagues, and build out the wider biostatistics function as the portfolio grows.


🍊 About you

We'd like to hear from you if…

  • PhD in statistics or biostatistics with 10+ years' relevant pharma/biotech experience, or MS with 15+ years, including lead statistician experience across multiple Phase I/II programmes (Phase III and CSR experience a plus)

  • Personally interacted with health authorities on at least one programme, ideally an early-phase IND (NDA also acceptable), including formal meetings or written correspondence; FDA preferred, EMA also considered. Adaptive trial design experience required

  • Experience setting statistical strategy at a programme or portfolio level, with strong knowledge of CDISC standards, regulatory submission requirements, and current drug development trends

  • Excellent programming skills, including independently generating analysis output; R and/or SAS fluency preferred, and familiarity with applying AI/ML tools to statistical workflows a plus

  • Experience evaluating external clinical data through due diligence, licensing, or M&A activity is a plus

🍊 What you'll focus on

  • Lead statistician on active programmes: Personally lead the statistics on active and incoming programmes, from protocol development through database lock and clinical study report - authoring and reviewing SAPs, sample size and power calculations, and randomisation schemes, and reviewing output at key milestones including interim analyses and DSMB packages.

  • Regulatory representation: Serve as the primary statistical voice with regulators - meetings, briefing documents, and responses to health authority queries - and author and review the statistical sections of regulatory submissions, including IND and NDA filings.

About Us

Basecamp Research is building frontier AI for therapeutic design. We believe the future of medicine lies in reprogramming the body to repair itself, and we design the models and the medicines to teach it how.

Our EDEN models are trained on BaseData, the world's largest proprietary genomic dataset, with over 10B genes collected through partnerships in more than 30 countries across all seven continents. This gives our AI models access to genetic diversity that doesn't exist in public databases, and enables EDEN to design cell and gene therapies, enzymes, and peptides directly from information about a disease. Our pipeline of EDEN-designed therapeutics, beginning with in vivo cell therapy, is advancing towards clinical development.

In September 2026 we closed an oversubscribed $140M Series C led by S32, with participation from NVIDIA, Anthropic's Anthology Fund, Catalio, European Tech Collective, Firebrand River Capital, King Philanthropies, NATO Innovation Fund, NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm), Redalpine, Rockefeller Foundation, Singular, Sovereign AI and True Ventures. At Basecamp Research, we pride ourselves on being a lean collaborative and global team with extremely specialist and unique skills. Our biologists, engineers, ML scientists and field explorers are united by a sense of adventure and the belief that AI, biology and data, will result in new medicines for patients who have few options today.

The hands of the Trillion Gene Atlas. You will keep samples moving through our extraction, normalisation, and library preparation pipeline - precisely, reliably, and at pace.

  • Maintain a safe, organised lab environment. Uphold high standards of lab hygiene, reagent management, and safety compliance including CL2 working practices. Help keep the lab stocked, organised, and ready to run at scale.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Hands-on laboratory experience in a molecular biology or life sciences setting - academic, commercial, or both

  • Practical experience with DNA extraction from biological or environmental samples using kit-based and automated methods

  • Comfortable working at high throughput with strong attention to detail - precise pipetting, consistent technique, reliable record-keeping

  • Ability to follow SOPs accurately, identify deviations, and escalate clearly and promptly

  • Experience with environmental or metagenomic sample types - soils, sediments, faecal, or other challenging matrices

  • A curiosity about sequencing technology and genuine interest in learning and growing within a fast-moving team

You'll bring real depth in metagenomic extraction methodologies and the ability to recover usable nucleic acids from difficult, low-biomass or inhibitor-rich matrices. You'll understand when good is good enough and can support handover for testing and implementation in production.

Your work will contribute directly to Basecamp Research’s Trillion Gene Atlas Project, helping transform diverse global samples into high-quality biological data that can reveal new genes, proteins, pathways, and functions from nature.

The role is laboratory based but you will have ownership over your projects, with the opportunity to work closely with our Collaborations team who coordinate sample collection globally, and to have input into the methods for collection or extraction and the molecular biology methods that are applied to a global network of collaborators, seeing your work make an impact in real-time.

The role will suit someone with experience who enjoys the technically focused aspects of development, from rapid prototyping to delivery. You'll also have the opportunity to work with the Data teams, who may have specific requirements for particular targeted methods, all with the aim of increasing our database diversity, data quality and scalability. Our biologists, engineers, ML scientists and field explorers are united by a sense of adventure and the belief that AI, biology and data, will result in new medicines for patients who have few options today.

The Role

We are looking for a Bioinformatics Scientist to join our Genomics team in London. You will turn vast, heterogeneous, often downright strange biological data into annotated, trustworthy resources the rest of the company and our models can build on.

We are building biological datasets at a scale no reference database has approached. Our flagship effort, the Trillion Gene Atlas, is one of the largest long-read sequencing efforts to date, targeting a trillion genes and a quadrillion assembled nucleotides.

The heart of this role is understanding the data itself. Much of what we collect doesn't fit existing schemas or tools, so the job is not to just run a standard toolchain but to develop new methods that label and mine biology no one has characterised before. Because you understand both the biology and what the models need downstream, you know what the data has to become, not just correct but machine-readable and model-ready.

  • Analyse diverse, messy biological datatypes, primarily microbiomes from a wide range of sample types, spanning both prokaryotes and eukaryotes, bringing the biological judgment to know when an annotation is a real signal versus an artefact.

  • Reach for newer ML methods where they are the right tool for annotation, labelling, or mining, and fold them into your approach cleanly.

  • Keep the data trustworthy. Provenance, edge cases, and data integrity are part of the craft, not an afterthought.

  • Help build outward-facing tools where the opportunity arises. For example, a predictive "oracle" that helps our field teams target regions of the planet where undiscovered biodiversity is most likely to be found, turning curated data back into smarter sampling and discovery.

You have a deep understanding of biological data and a strong core in sequence informatics (alignment, annotation, sequence analysis), with the judgment to know when standard tools are misleading or not right for the job. When a tool or method doesn't exist, your instinct is to build one - and the tools and methods you've built have been applied to real data at scale.

You've curated data that went on to train real models or feed large-scale analyses. You're a capable enough engineer to make your methods real, but you treat engineering as the means, not the mission.

You like to move fast, to ship, learn, and iterate at pace, without cutting corners on rigour.

You are excited by the scale of the biology: genetic diversity that exists in no public database, and the chance to invent the methods that make it usable for the first time.

You'll likely have a PhD in a relevant field, an MSc with 1-3 years of relevant experience, or a BSc with 3 or more.

jobs.description:
About Niantic Spatial

At Niantic Spatial, we're building the future of physical AI. Powered by a proprietary database of over 30 billion posed images, our groundbreaking mapping technology unlocks a new dimension of interaction and spatial intelligence that helps both humans and machines better understand, represent, navigate, and engage with the real environment.

Our reconstruction technology captures environments with geometric accuracy and extreme detail from any standard camera, and our Visual Positioning System delivers precise positioning almost anywhere in the world. We serve customers across robotics, the public sector, and energy and industrial markets - building for the 80% of economic activity that takes place beyond our screens.

About the Role

Niantic Spatial makes the physical world computable, helping people and machines collaborate safely by aligning how they understand reality. One of the fundamental problems we're helping autonomy teams and engineers overcome is the sim-to-real gap for visual-spatial understanding. We're applying our team's decades of experience encoding the world precisely as it is at Google Maps, Google Earth, and Niantic Labs to build the scalable real-to-sim stack for embodied AI.

Niantic Spatial's R&D Team in London is seeking a Research Scientist to push the frontiers of Spatial AI, advancing our Large Geospatial Model as a dedicated member of the Embodied AI group. You will invent and develop algorithms and systems that sit at the cross-section of computer vision, machine learning, AI, graphics, and robotics.

We're passionate about discovery, so we're looking for scientists who want to learn, publish, teach, and deploy every new invention.

What You'll Do

  • Develop New Spatial Representations - Develop new spatial representations that embodied AI can learn from, train in, and act on.

  • Advance Real-to-Sim Pipelines - Advance real-to-sim pipelines connecting real-world observations, 3D reconstruction, simulation, and robotic policy learning.

  • Solve Emerging Spatial Problems - Solve emerging problems that relate to spatial intelligence, 3D scene representation, training data, model efficiency, and interactive systems.

  • Take Capabilities Through to Evidence - Take new capabilities through to evidence: what changed for the policy, not only what changed in the reconstruction.

  • Build Prototypes - Build proof of concept prototypes, initially for internal use, where some will need to run at production scale on customer data.

  • Collaborate Across Research and Product - Collaborate closely with researchers, engineers, and product partners to bring novel models to production.

  • Publish Your Work - Publish and present your work.

What You'll Bring

  • A PhD in computer vision, robotics, graphics, machine learning, or a related field, or equivalent research experience, with a publication record at top venues.

  • Substantial expertise in robotics or embodied AI, including experience in sim-to-real transfer, domain randomization, policy evaluation, and simulation-based learning.

  • Deep experience with 3D scene representations: Gaussian splatting, neural fields, meshes, point clouds, or implicit representations.

  • You have applied generative or diffusion models to 3D data, such as scene completion, inpainting, relighting, or novel view synthesis from sparse capture.

  • You have worked on 3D semantics, open-vocabulary scene understanding, or scene graphs.

  • Proficiency in Python and Deep Learning libraries such as PyTorch.

  • GPU or graphics programming experience, such as custom CUDA kernels, shaders, or differentiable rendering.

  • A track record of contributing to widely used open-source research codebases.

Nice to Have

  • Proficiency in C++.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary range of £103,500 to £202,500. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.

This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office.

jobs.title: Network Developer
jobs.description:
Senior Network Developer

About Share

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months.

Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served.

The Role

Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.

You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.

What you'll do

  • Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.

  • Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.

  • Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.

  • Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.

  • Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.

  • Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.

  • Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.

  • Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.

Our Ideal Candidate

  • 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP.

  • Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit.

  • Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense.

  • Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.

  • You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe.

  • You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed.

  • AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't.

  • You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network.

  • A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders.

Nice to have

  • Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale.

  • Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them.

  • Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling.

  • 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification.

  • Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it.

  • Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America.

  • DDoS mitigation at the edge.

If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway.

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a venture-backed company (US-incorporated, with a Kenya operating entity)

jobs.title: Network Operation Engineer
jobs.description:
Network Operations Engineer

1. About the role

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it.

For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar.

We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling.

The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes.

You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it.

2. What you'll do

Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing.

Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with.

Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state.

Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online.

Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed.

Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift.

Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far.

3. Who we're looking for

A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for.

Must-have

  • Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong.

  • Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told.

  • Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge.

  • Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus.

  • Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you.

  • Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher.

  • Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly.

  • Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time.

  • Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day.

Nice-to-have

  • CCNP, or MikroTik MTCNA / MTCRE.

  • Prior NOC, ISP, or carrier operations experience.

  • Hands on with MPLS (L3VPN, EVPN) and the multi-tenant isolation a shared backbone needs.

  • Exposure to open source and white box routing or forwarding stacks (SONiC, IP Infusion OcNOS, FRR, or similar).

  • Network source of truth and automation tooling (Nautobot, NAPALM, Jinja config generation, NETCONF or gNMI).

  • Familiarity with a monitoring stack such as Zabbix, Grafana, Loki, or Prometheus, and with flow telemetry.

  • Working familiarity with FreeRADIUS, CoA and Disconnect flows, and how session control and accounting hook into the network.

  • Exposure to applying ML or AI in network operations: anomaly detection, predictive failure analysis, automated triage or remediation.

  • IPv6 and dual stack exposure, and internet exchange operations (looking glass and route server behaviour, IRR and RPKI hygiene).

4. What we offer

  • A seat inside a serious, very senior network team, with people who have deep service provider backgrounds and will sharpen you fast. You will see how a real carrier network behaves under live conditions.

  • A front row seat to how a network actually gets run in 2026. Open source forwarding, config as code, and an LLM layer doing real operational work. Not a slide about the future of network operations, but the environment you would work in every shift, and help build.

  • Real engineering, not just monitoring. The role is built so the quiet hours go into automation, propagation and health work, and tickets off the board. The path into deeper network engineering and automation work is the plan, not a vague someday.

  • Competitive salary and private health and wellness benefits, fully remote, in a mission driven, investor backed company building the backbone of Africa's next generation internet.

Bei VREY bauen wir das EnergyOS für Mehrfamilienhäuser.

In Deutschland stehen über 3,3 Millionen Mehrparteienhäuser – und sie sind das schwarze Loch der Energiewende. <1% Solardurchdringung. <2% Smart Metering. Kaum Flexibilität oder intelligentes Energiemanagement.

Gleichzeitig zwingt die Regulierung Eigentümer zu massiven Investitionen: Solar wird zur Pflicht, Smart Meter müssen in den nächsten 5 Jahren flächendeckend ausgerollt werden, Heizung und Mobilität elektrifizieren sich. Das Mehrfamilienhaus wird vom Betongold zum aktiven Teil der dezentralen Energieinfrastruktur.

Was fehlt, ist ein integriertes System, das diesen Wandel wirtschaftlich und operativ beherrschbar macht.

VREY kombiniert zertifizierten Messstellenbetrieb mit eigener Software und ermöglicht Eigentümern erstmals, ihren selbst erzeugten Solarstrom direkt an ihre Mieter zu verkaufen – einfach und ohne selbst zum Energieversorger zu werden (§42b EnWG).

Damit wird regulatorischer Zwang zu einer profitablen und planbaren Chance:

jobs.title: Automation Engineer, Wet Lab
jobs.description:
Role summary:

At Differential Bio, our mission is to unlock the potential of the bioeconomy by fixing how biological R&D and scale-up are done.

Today, bioprocess development is slow, expensive, and limited by the economics of lab hardware. A typical system runs 4, 8, or 24 bioreactors in parallel, and a single run can cost anywhere from hundreds to several thousand dollars. Our ambition is different: 100 parallel bioreactor runs at around $10 per run.

Why does that matter? Because radically reducing the cost per insight changes what is possible. Instead of running a handful of carefully selected experiments, we can generate dense, standardized datasets across thousands of conditions.

That data is at the core of Differential Bio. First, we automate high-throughput data generation. Then we use our proprietary datasets to train AI models that understand how bioprocesses behave across conditions and scales - with the long-term goal of building a digital twin of fermentation at any scale.

We have already built two end-to-end automated fermentation pods that operate continuously and generate experimental data every week. Being vertically integrated all the way down to the physical lab has proven to be a major advantage for us.

Now we are hiring the first role dedicated entirely to lab automation. You will take over this domain from our founder and CTO, Martin, report directly to him, and own how our automation platform develops from here.

This is, in many ways, the role we always wished existed: high autonomy, genuinely difficult engineering problems, the freedom and resources to solve them properly, and a mission worth the hard work.

This is not a role for someone who wants to select the next six-figure laboratory automation system from a catalogue. We want someone who looks at a €500,000 solution and asks: Why does this cost €500,000? What problem are we actually solving? And could we achieve the same outcome - or a better one - for a fraction of the cost and at 10x the scale?

Sometimes the answer will be an established lab instrument. Sometimes it will be an industrial robot, a €50 sensor, a 3D-printed part, and some clever engineering.

Your opportunity is to help us completely rethink how lab automation is done and build the infrastructure that makes biological R&D dramatically faster and cheaper.

Key responsibilities:

  • Own lab automation at Differential Bio end-to-end, from creating individual components to developing complete new automated fermentation systems, including technical decisions, experimentation, suppliers, and budget.

  • Drive our ambition to dramatically increase experimental density while reducing the cost per experiment and cost per insight.

  • Translate wet-lab workflows into reliable, scalable automation together with our scientists, software engineers, and ML engineers.

  • Make pragmatic build vs. buy vs. modify decisions instead of defaulting to expensive, closed laboratory automation platforms.

  • Prototype and build yourself: fermentation pods and small bioreactors, using 3D printing & our workshop.

  • Evaluate and integrate robots, liquid handling systems, and emerging automation technologies, working directly with manufacturers to adapt or co-develop around our requirements.

  • Continuously improve reliability, throughput, maintainability, and cost as our automation platform scales.

Qualifications:

We care more about how you solve engineering problems than about a specific degree or career path.

You should:

  • Have evidence of excellence: 4+ years of experience in lab automation, robotics, or other automation projects involving real hardware - or an equivalent track record of serious hobby projects where you have built, modified, automated, and debugged physical systems yourself.

  • Be a tinkerer: someone who enjoys opening the box, understanding how something works, modifying it, and building something better when necessary.

  • Be comfortable with robotics, sensors, actuators, mechanical design, electronics, embedded systems, or related technologies.

  • Be able to move quickly between disciplines and collaborate with wet-lab scientists, automation specialists, software engineers, and ML engineers.

  • Be comfortable with ambiguity and high autonomy. We define outcomes; you have substantial freedom to determine how to achieve them.

  • Combine creative engineering with a strong focus on reliability and repeatability.

Experience with laboratory automation, bioreactors, liquid handling, CAD, 3D printing, Python, PLCs, machine vision, or industrial automation is a plus - but not a requirement.

This is a demanding job. The problems are hard, the ownership is real, and there will not always be a playbook to follow. We are looking for someone who enjoys that responsibility rather than avoids it. We want to see the fire in you: the curiosity, energy, and determination to keep digging until something works.

Benefits:

  • High ownership: Own our lab automation stack, technical direction, suppliers, and significant parts of the automation budget.

  • Real freedom to build: We have 3D printers, workshop capabilities, testing space, and the budget to buy robots and hardware when experimentation requires it.

Holidu connects 4 million guests with 55k+ vacation rental hosts every year. Our Agentic Experience team is a small, fast-moving group inside Holidu's 200-person Engineering organization, rethinking how users interact with our platform using AI, how we build applications, and how we design agentic systems, with a lot of first-principles thinking along the way.

jobs.description:
Über Holidu

Holidu ist eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Tech-Unternehmen für Ferienvermietung weltweit. Unser Ziel: Ferienunterkünfte sollen sich sorgenfrei buchen und vermieten lassen und dabei einfach Freude machen. Dafür helfen wir Gastgeber*innen, mit weniger Aufwand mehr Buchungen zu erzielen, und Gästen, genau die Ferienunterkunft zu finden, in der sie sich rundum wohlfühlen. Bei uns arbeiten rund 700 Kolleg*innen aus über 60 Nationen. Uns verbinden die Leidenschaft für Technologie, der Anspruch, jeden Tag ein Stück besser zu werden, und der Antrieb, mehr als 40.000 Gastgeber*innen und 4 Millionen Gästen im Jahr das bestmögliche Erlebnis zu bieten.

Dein Team

Unser Finance-Team kümmert sich um die Zahlen hinter der schnell wachsenden Reiseplattform. In der Buchhaltung sind wir rund 15 Kolleg*innen und verantworten aktuell mehr als zehn Gesellschaften im In- und Ausland, Tendenz steigend. Bei uns lernst du das Handwerk der Buchhaltung von erfahrenen Kolleg*innen von Grund auf und übernimmst Schritt für Schritt mehr Verantwortung; in welche Richtung, das gestaltest du mit deinen Stärken und Interessen. Weil wir wirklich als Team arbeiten, kommt der Spaß dabei nicht zu kurz, im Alltag wie bei unseren Teamevents.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du übernimmst Aufgaben der Finanzbuchhaltung, insbesondere in der Kreditorenbuchhaltung im operativen Tagesgeschäft: du bearbeitest unser Buchhaltungspostfach, erfasst und verbuchst Rechnungen, bereitest Zahlläufe vor, unterstützt bei der laufenden Kontenabstimmung und -pflege und klärst kleinere Differenzen zunehmend selbstständig.

  • Du wirkst bei unseren Monats- und Jahresabschlüssen mit.

  • Du unterstützt bei Projekten zum Beispiel bei der Prozessoptimierung in der Buchhaltung

  • Du hilfst mit, unsere Buchhaltung Schritt für Schritt schlauer zu machen, zum Beispiel mit Excel oder KI.

  • Du entwickelst dich Schritt für Schritt weiter und gestaltest deine Zukunft bei uns aktiv mit.

 

Dein Profil

  • Du hast eine abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung, z. B. als Steuerfachangestellte*r, oder ein betriebswirtschaftliches Studium mit Schwerpunkt Finanzbuchhaltung / Rechnungswesen.

  • Du hast bereits erste Berufserfahrung in der Buchhaltung gesammelt, zum Beispiel im Rahmen deiner Ausbildung, eines Praktikums oder einer Werkstudententätigkeit.

  • Du bringst gute Kenntnisse in der Rechnungslegung mit und kennst die Grundlagen der Buchhaltung; in neue Themen arbeitest du dich mit Freude ein.

  • Du arbeitest sicher mit Excel

  • Kenntnisse von Buchhaltungssystemen wie SAP sind von Vorteil

  • Du bist offen für den Einsatz von KI und hast Freude daran, wiederkehrende Aufgaben schlauer zu lösen.

  • Du arbeitest verlässlich, genau und strukturiert, bringst analytisches Denken mit und schaust gerne über den Tellerrand, um bestehende Prozesse zu hinterfragen und zu verbessern.

  • Du hast Spaß an der Arbeit in einem dynamischen, schnellen Umfeld und bringst Eigenmotivation und Einsatzbereitschaft mit, um wirklich etwas zu bewegen.

  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch (mindestens C1 Level) und gut Englisch.

 

Was wir sonst noch bieten

  • Lernen: Wachse in einer Arbeitskultur, die von Neugier und offenem Feedback lebt. Lerne von unseren herausragenden Kolleg*innen, arbeite disziplinübergreifend zusammen und profitiere von Mentoring und persönlichen Lernbudgets – mit einem besonderen Fokus auf KI.

  • Flexibilität: Genieße die Vorteile eines hybriden Arbeitsmodells mit mindestens 50% Bürozeit für persönliche Zusammenarbeit und arbeite bis zu 8 Wochen im Jahr von anderen inspirierenden Orten aus. Bleibe durch regelmäßige Veranstaltungen und Meetups über unsere fast 30 Büros hinweg verbunden.

  • Tolle Leute: Werde Teil eines Teams aus smarten, motivierten und internationalen Kolleg*innen, die sich gegenseitig fordern und unterstützen. jobs.title: Technical Pre-sales Solution Engineer (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
Role Overview

As a Technical Pre-sales Solution Engineer (EMS, PPC & SCADA) at NeuVerge-Tron GmbH, you will serve as the technical lead and solution architect during pre-sales and tender phases for utility-scale renewable energy and energy storage power plants.

In this position, your core product portfolio comprises Energy Management Systems (EMS), Power Plant Controllers (PPC), and SCADA platforms. You will analyze customer requirements, regional Grid Codes, and Transmission/Distribution System Operator (TSO/DSO) mandates, translating them into resilient, high-availability, and cybersecure system architectures.

(Note: This role focuses on control software, industrial automation, and OT system architecture; it does not cover battery cell sizing, containerized mechanical design, or civil EPC scope.)

 

Key Responsibilities

Technical Pre-sales & Bid Management

  • Analyze customer technical specifications, RFIs, RFQs, and RFPs for utility-scale solar, wind, and hybrid BESS assets.

  • Author technical proposals, functional architecture diagrams, and Statements of Work (SOW) for EMS/SCADA solutions.

  • Compile compliance matrices and deviation lists addressing customer specifications and utility regulations.

  • Define the Bill of Materials (BOM), covering server hardware, industrial controllers, networking equipment, software licenses, and engineering services.

  • Lead technical deep-dive workshops, solution demonstrations, and clarification sessions with customers, EPC contractors, and grid operators.

Grid Code Compliance & Functional Control Design

  • Evaluate regional Grid Code regulations across target European markets (e.g., VDE-AR-N 4110/4120, ENTSO-E standards) and translate them into EMS/PPC control requirements

  • Architect plant-level control logic, including Active Power Control, Reactive Power/Power Factor Regulation, POI/PCC Voltage Support, Frequency Response, and Ramp Rate restrictions.

  • Define EMS-level operational strategies, such as automated dispatch tracking, State of Charge (SoC) management constraints, energy arbitrage scheduling, ancillary service controls, and fail-safe/black-start logics.

System Integration & Communication Architecture

  • Design overall system architectures connecting EMS, PPC, SCADA, Historian, and Human-Machine Interfaces (HMI).

  • Define interface specifications for external subsystems: Battery Management Systems (BMS), Power Conversion Systems (PCS), MV switchgear, digital protection relays, power meters, and TSO/DSO dispatch centers.

  • Develop and maintain interface control documents (ICD), data point lists, and signal mapping registers.

  • Implement and validate standard industrial protocols, including Modbus TCP/RTU, IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850 (MMS/GOOSE), DNP3, and OPC UA.

  • Architect high-availability schemes, redundancy topologies, automated failover mechanisms, time synchronization (NTP/PTP), and disaster recovery plans.

OT Networking & Cybersecurity Architecture

  • Design Operational Technology (OT) network topologies, VLAN segmentations, IP addressing schemes, and DMZ firewall policies.

  • Formulate secure remote maintenance topologies, jump host concepts, VPN tunnels, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) mechanisms.

  • Ensure EMS solution adherence to cybersecurity standards, including IEC 62443 and IEC 62351 frameworks.

  • Collaborate with customer IT/OT security teams and external auditors during security reviews and threat modeling assessments.

Verification & Handover

  • Define verification scopes and technical criteria for Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), and grid compliance commissioning.

  • Support engineering, commissioning, and project management teams during post-award handover to ensure seamless project delivery.

 

Scope Boundaries

  • To preserve focus on control systems and software integration, this position explicitly excludes:

  • Battery cell/module selection, chemistry evaluation, and electrochemical degradation modeling.

  • Mechanical layout, thermal HVAC design, or fire suppression engineering of BESS containers.

  • Primary high/medium voltage electrical hardware engineering (transformers, switchgear internals, or EPC civil infrastructure).

 

Qualifications & Profile

Education:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Automation, Power Systems, Computer Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.

Professional Experience:

  • 3 to 5+ years of experience in technical presales, solution architecture, or systems engineering focusing on EMS, PPC, or SCADA in power generation or grid utilities.

  • Practical familiarity with grid integration procedures and technical dialogue with European grid operators (TSOs/DSOs).

Technical & Protocol Competencies:

  • Solid understanding of power utility communication standards: IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850, Modbus TCP/RTU, DNP3, and OPC UA.

  • Hands-on experience with industrial automation platforms (PLCs/RTUs), real-time historians, and SCADA packages.

  • Working knowledge of industrial cybersecurity best practices (IEC 62443 / IEC 62351).

Key Competencies:

  • Strong analytical capability to dissect technical tender documents into structured requirements.

  • Confident presentation skills in customer-facing technical exchanges and contract negotiations.

Language Skills:

  • Professional fluency in English (written and verbal) is required.

  • German language or any other third EU or Chinese proficiency are strongly preferred.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer, Shopping Agents
jobs.description:
Senior Backend Engineer, Shopping Agents

Sage AI Labs · Munich · Full-time · [Remote]

About us

Sage AI Labs is building the infrastructure that lets AI agents transact on the open web. It is one of the few genuinely unsolved problems left in commerce, and whoever solves it sets the defaults everyone else builds on top of.

The company was founded by Sebastian Thrun (founder of Google X and Waymo, Udacity) and is backed by leading venture and strategic investors.

About the role

We build agents that shop for you. They find products across the open web and complete the purchase end to end. Real carts, real payments, and real systems built to stop them.

You would own that. Architecture, code, deploys, monitoring, and on-call for systems that transact around the clock, working directly with our CTO.

What you'll own

Our checkout agents. Frontier-model computer-use agents driving live checkouts at scale, plus the machinery that keeps them standing when the ground moves. Every retailer breaks differently and they change without warning. Your job is to make failure rare and recovery automatic.

Ingestion at scale. Take product ingestion from hundreds of sources to thousands. The answer is not more hand-written code. It is infrastructure that generates, validates, and monitors itself.

Search and ranking. Embedding-based retrieval, LLM query understanding, reranking, and caching, across a catalog that never stops changing.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years building backend and infrastructure systems, with strong Python

  • You have owned production systems end to end: deploys, databases, observability, and the pager. You have been the person who got paged, and you fixed the class of problem rather than the incident

  • You like adversarial problems. Systems where something on the other side is actively working against you

  • You take correctness seriously because the stakes are real. These systems spend customers' money, so a silent failure is a wrong order, not a red build

  • You can move without a finished spec. We are small, and the roadmap changes when the market does

Nice to have

  • Built AI-first products or LLM-based agents in production, not just in a prototype

  • Working knowledge of classic ML and deep learning, enough to reason about retrieval and ranking rather than only calling an API

  • Background in e-commerce, payments, or fraud and risk infrastructure

Why this role

Very few engineers get to own a category-defining system while the category is still being defined. This is one of those seats, at the point where it still counts as early. A year from now this problem will have a standard answer and someone will have written it. We intend for that to be us.

That is why we have been driving the mobility and energy transition for nearly a decade. Through transformation projects that accelerate digitalization and position organizations for the future. We rethink organizations, put technology at the center, and always keep the people in mind. For us, change is not a matter of will, but of the ability to continuously evolve.

Together with our ventures &amp and accilium ventures, we operate at seven locations in Germany, Austria, Poland, and Romania and employ 110 people. According to Statista and brand eins, accilium ranks among the best management consultancies in the German-speaking world and is part of the “Hidden Champion of Consulting 2026/27”.

Why launch your career at accilium?

At accilium, you will help build something big. We move fast – and we will take you along on our journey working with top-tier clients and engaging in diverse projects. We foster an open team culture, place the highest value on your professional development, and always meet on equal footing.

You will work on one of the largest transformation programs in the automotive industry, supporting one of the world's leading automotive OEMs. Our projects focus on areas where engineering, product data, and vehicle software are being fundamentally transformed, ranging from the harmonization of engineering and IT landscapes to Software-Defined Vehicles (SDV) and the entire automotive value chain.

These initiatives come with complex challenges. Target architectures must be aligned across brands, domains, and numerous stakeholders while remaining stable over time. Legacy systems must be replaced in a structured way while business operations continue uninterrupted. At the same time, software-centric development approaches are changing established processes and responsibilities. We ensure that architecture and implementation are aligned, decisions are well prepared, and progress remains transparent.

Together with your project team, you will take ownership of customer challenges from day one. You can always rely on leadership support, coaching, and continuous feedback to accelerate your development. We believe in full transparency when it comes to your career. Your progression all the way to Senior Consultant in the Automotive Practice is determined solely by your individual performance.

Your responsibilities

You will work closely with the project team and project management and quickly take ownership of your own workstreams.

  • Target Vision & Dependencies: Support the development of target architectures and roadmaps while creating transparency regarding dependencies across topics, teams, and systems.

  • Transition Management: Support the migration from legacy systems and processes into future-state target architectures, including business cases and transition planning.

  • Requirements & Decision Management: Maintain requirements and prioritization structures, document decisions, and keep key project artifacts up to date.

  • Analysis: Analyze existing system and process landscapes and develop decision papers and business cases.

  • Tracking & Reporting: Build progress dashboards and reporting structures and prepare management reports.

  • Presentation & Facilitation: Create concise decision-making materials and increasingly facilitate workshops and alignment sessions with business and IT stakeholders.

  • Project Management: Apply project management methodologies and structure content and interdependencies within the overall project framework.

  • Functional Consulting: Develop concepts and provide consulting support as a trusted sparring partner for the client.

What is in it for you?

SALARY

  • Full‑time monthly gross salary starting at € 4.650 (including 30 vacation days), depending on your experience and qualifications.

  • Annual salary increase + bonus (up to one month’s gross salary or 10 additional vacation days).

Because we value your commitment.

CAREER PATH & DEVELOPMENT

  • 100% transparent career path (company-wide standard) + Individual People Year instead of fixed promotion cycles.

  • A People Partner who provides guidance on career direction and development focus from day one.

  • Professional training, internal training formats, semi-annual performance reviews, and management 1:1s to accelerate your learning curve from day one.

  • Regular feedback, direct access to partnership, and a culture of change to foster your growth.

Your career and development are a priority.

IMPACT & VISIBILITY

  • We are big enough to deliver real impact, yet agile enough for everyone to actively shape the future.

  • AI is part of our daily work. We implement AI for our clients and grow internally to achieve our goal of becoming an AI‑first consultancy.

You witness real change and authentic decision‑making processes.

ONBOARDING

  • Buddy will assist you with onboarding and introduces you to our resources, organizational structure, and tools.

  • Latest hardware and software: Surface, iPhone & home‑office equipment available from day one.

Structured onboarding for a smooth start.

COMMUNITY & BENEFITS

  • Public transport ticket & corporate benefits.

  • 80/20 smart working rule (1 home office day per week available).

  • Events like reTreat, acc’sPerience, and our Christmas party create real connection.

  • Office breakfasts and after‑work gatherings strengthen the local community and encourage exchange.

  • Work from Anywhere option for flexible work models (up to 10 days per year from within Europe).

At accilium, community is real - not just a buzzword.

What makes a great fit

YOUR QUALIFICATIONS

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Systems Engineering, Automotive Engineering, Industrial Engineering with a technical or IT focus, Business Informatics, or a comparable field of study.

  • Experience: At least one internship or working student position with a reputable management consultancy. Additional experience with an automotive manufacturer or supplier is an advantage.

  • Technical Understanding: Foundational knowledge of Systems Engineering, IT Architecture, or engineering and product data processes, gained through your specialization, thesis work, or practical experience.

  • Analytics & Tools: Strong proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, combined with an interest in structured data analysis and visualization.

  • Good to have: Experience with Jira and Confluence, basic knowledge of Enterprise Architecture Management (EAM) or TOGAF, and familiarity with agile frameworks such as Scrum and SAFe.

  • Languages: Excellent German and English skills (at least C1 level).*

    *Global scale - Table 1 (CEFR 3.3): Common Reference levels (coe.int)

We’re looking for someone who is passionate about consulting and eager to deep‑dive into the consulting field.

YOUR APPROACH

  • Growth Mindset: Curiosity, a commitment to continuous learning, and the willingness to go the extra mile during demanding project phases.

  • Industry Passion: A genuine enthusiasm for the automotive industry, ideally demonstrated through internships, working student positions, thesis work, or extracurricular activities such as Formula Student.

  • Soft Skills: Strong communication and problem-solving capabilities, combined with flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic, stakeholder-rich environment.

  • Willingness to Travel: Flexibility to travel within the DACH region (depending on specific project needs).

At accilium, we nurture your personal growth and provide guidance every step of the way.

Why accilium?

accilium is an award-winning strategy and management consultancy shaping the future of mobility and energy. Driven by a strong mission, we prioritize teamwork and continuous learning. Our growing team of more than 110 experts has become a rising star in the consulting industry, and we are excited about the increasing attention we are receiving. 

 

If you want to be part of building something great, click “Apply” or reach out to Anna Evinová (.

 

accilium is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace, regardless of origin, religion, sexual identity, gender, age, or belief. This policy applies to all employment practices within our company. accilium makes hiring decisions solely based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

With your expertise in real-time communication, embedded systems, and industrial networks, you’ll lay the foundation for high-performance, reliable, and future-proof automation solutions.



What can you expect?

  • Help shape the next generation of intelligent IoT solutions by developing innovative software for open communication protocols and TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) technologies on new and existing embedded platforms

Your profile

  • In-depth knowledge of Ethernet-based communication protocols such as TCP/IP, TLS, and PTP; ideally supplemented by experience with industry standards such as IEEE 1588, TSN, and X.509

  • Strong conceptual and analytical skills, as well as the ability to communicate complex technical issues to various stakeholders in a way that is tailored to their needs, understandable, and practical

What are your benefits?

  • Personal and professional development: Individual mentoring and coaching, ACADEMY training courses, and an open feedback culture
  • Attractive career opportunities: Transparent career paths, the opportunity to take on responsibility quickly, and international career prospects
  • Performance-based compensation package: Fixed and variable salary components as well as assessments every six months

jobs.title: Trainee (m/w/d) in der energetischen Sanierung
jobs.description:
Deine Rolle

Wenn du dich für Projektmanagement, vertriebliches Denken, viel Kundenkontakt und einen abwechslungsreichen Alltag begeistern kannst und noch den perfekten Karrierestart suchst, dann bist du bei unserem Traineeship genau richtig. Durch eine umfassende Betreuung von deinem Mentor wirst du in alle Themen aus dem Sanierungsmanagement eingearbeitet, bis du so weit bist, deine eigenen Projekte leiten zu können. Wir bringen dir alles bei, was du wissen musst. Alles was du mitbringen musst, ist eine große Portion Antrieb und Interesse an unserer Branche.


Deine Mission

Du lernst im Rahmen unseres 12-monatigen Traineeprogramms alle Bereiche kennen, die Du für die Umsetzung einer professionellen Sanierung benötigst.

  • Du berätst unsere Kund:innen zu ihren Sanierungsvorhaben und verkaufst unsere Leistung
  • Du versorgst deine Kolleg:innen in der Energieberatung mit Informationen
  • Du planst die Umsetzung zusammen mit unseren Handwerkspartnern
  • Du sorgst für einen reibungslosen Ablauf und Abschluss der Sanierung
  • Du arbeitest mit hochwertigen Anfragen, denn bei uns gibt es keine Kaltakquise


Dein Profil

  • Du begeisterst Dich für Immobilien und deren energetisch sinnvolle Sanierung
  • Du hast eine Ausbildung oder ein Studium abgeschlossen
  • Erste Berufserfahrung in der Immobilien-/ Baubranche oder im Handwerk ist ein Plus
  • Du gehst offen auf Kund:innen zu und sprichst die Sprache des Handwerks
  • Hohe Zuverlässigkeit und Verantwortungsbewusstsein
  • Als Teamplayer trägst Du zum Erfolg der Niederlassung bei
  • Du hast einen Führerschein, gute Fahrpraxis und bist gerne unterwegs
  • Du sprichst und schreibst die deutsche Sprache fehlerfrei, um gekonnt mit unterschiedlichen Zielgruppen zu kommunizieren 


Warum RENEWA?

  • Transparentes Verdienstmodell: Profitiere von einer fairen Provisionsregelung 
  • Echte Erfahrung: Du arbeitest nicht für die Schublade, sondern an realen Projekten
  • Steile Lernkurve: Wir nehmen uns Zeit, dir Dinge zu erklären - und lassen dich auch selbst machen
  • Gutes Team: Locker, hilfsbereit und ohne steife Hierarchien
  • Und danach? Wenn’s gut passt bleibst du bei uns
  • Moin: Du freust Dich auf eine mehrwöchige Einarbeitungsphase in Hamburg

jobs.title: AI Growth Marketer (m/w/d) - remote
jobs.description:
Deine Rolle

Wir sind ein kleines, agiles Marketing-Team. Jede und jeder übernimmt hier Ownership, entwickelt eigene Strategien und setzt sie selbst um. Seit wir konsequent mit AI arbeiten, sehen wir deutlich mehr Chancen zu wachsen, als wir bisher angehen können. Du verantwortest Growth-Projekte end-to-end, auf bestehenden Kanälen und auf neuen, die Du selbst findest. Du baust selbst, stellst selbst live in der App, im App Store oder auf der Website, und wertest die Daten danach aus. Die Wege sind kurz, der komplette Projektzyklus liegt bei Dir.

Deine Aufgaben:

  • Chancen in unseren Produkten finden. Du gehst regelmäßig durch Website, App Stores, Content, Jobboards und den Funnel bis Premium und findest die Stellen mit dem größten Hebel für Registrierungen und Umsatz.
  • Chancen im Markt erkennen. Du schaust genauso nach außen: Welche Trends und Plattformen bewegen unsere Zielgruppe gerade, welche Segmente oder Märkte lohnen einen Einstieg, welche Wachstumskanäle sollten wir aktivieren, die wir heute nicht nutzen, und was machen Wettbewerber.
  • Chancen bewerten und priorisieren. Du schätzt vorher ab, was realistisch drin ist und was es bringt, und bringst eine Shortlist ins Team. 
  • Selbst bauen und selbst live stellen. Du baust Landing Pages, Tests und Kampagnenbausteine mit AI und veröffentlichst sie selbst. Kein Ticket bei Engineering, kein Warten auf Design, keine Warteschlange. 
  • Testen und messen. Du setzt A/B-Tests auf der Website, in den App Stores und auf unseren weiteren Plattformen auf, wertest sie sauber aus und iterierst. 
  • App Store Optimisation. Du testest Screenshots, Icon, Titel und Beschreibungen laufend weiter.
  • Akquisition und früher Funnel. Dein Fokus liegt auf der Gewinnung neuer Nutzer. Gemeinsam mit dem Product Team bewertet Ihr, welche Zielgruppen und Kanäle den besten LTV bringen, und verbessert danach die Signup- und Activation-Flows im frühen Funnel.
  • Copy und Botschaften. Du formulierst, was StudySmarter Lernenden bringt, so dass es bei unserer Zielgruppe ankommt und konvertiert. Headlines auf Landing Pages, Ad-Copy, Video-Skripte, Plakatmotive und mehr. 
  • Content und Kampagnen mit AI. AI-Content-Projekte, Markenaufbau für unsere Jobboards, Out-of-Home-Kampagnen.
  • Love Brand aufbauen. Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns eine globale Love Brand für B2C und B2B und prägst mit, wie StudySmarter aussieht und klingt.


Was die Rolle nicht ist

  • Keine klassische Designstelle. Geschmack und Markenurteil sind wichtig, die handwerkliche Ausführung läuft über AI und Freelancer.
  • Kein Performance-Marketing-Job. Kanäle, Budget, Bidding und Attribution liegen an anderer Stelle im Team.
  • Keine Briefing-Rolle. Du machst die Arbeit selbst, statt sie weiterzugeben.
  • Keine Product-Rolle. Du bist kein Product Manager. Du trägst die Nutzerakquisition und arbeitest dafür eng mit dem Product Team zusammen, ohne Produktverantwortung zu übernehmen.
  • Keine Führungsrolle. Du arbeitest eng im Marketing-Team und gemeinsam mit dem Gründerteam, führst aber keine eigenen Mitarbeitenden. Dafür deutlich mehr Gestaltungsspielraum.


Was du für diese Rolle brauchst

  • Starke AI-Skills. Du arbeitest täglich mit AI-Tools wie Claude Code, Codex oder ähnlichen, dazu mit Agents und Automatisierung. Du baust eigene Seiten, Tools und Workflows und bringst sie selbst live, statt nur Prompts zu schreiben.
  • Starkes Copywriting und Storytelling. Du schreibst Texte, die auffallen und konvertieren, und findest die
    Worte, die bei Schülerinnen, Schülern und Studierenden ankommen. Du denkst in Geschichten und Nutzen, nicht in Feature-Listen.
  • Eigenständigkeit und Tempo. Du nimmst ein Thema und bringst es durch. Zehn Dinge live und gemessen sind Dir lieber als zwei perfekte. Zahlenverständnis. Du liest Funnel selbst, arbeitest in Analytics-Tools und bewertest Tests ehrlich, auch wenn
    das Ergebnis gegen Deine Idee spricht.
  • Ein Auge für Design. Du erkennst, was gut aussieht und was nicht, und kannst einschätzen, wann Design
    Conversion bringt und wann es nur Dekoration ist. Figma ist Dir vertraut.
  • Marketing-Grundverständnis. Du weißt, wie Paid, SEO und Lifecycle grundsätzlich funktionieren. Die Details der einzelnen Kanäle lernst Du bei uns.
Zwei Dinge sind Voraussetzung:
  • Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau. Du schreibst für unsere Zielgruppe auf Landing Pages, in
    Ads, in den App Stores und offline. Ohne echtes Sprachgefühl funktioniert das nicht.
  • Eigene Projekte, die Du zeigen kannst. Seiten, Tools, Content, Nebenprojekte. Das sagt uns
    mehr als ein Lebenslauf.

Wir schauen auf Skills, Execution, Tempo, Kreativität und Ambition, nicht auf die Anzahl der Berufsjahre. Starke
Absolventinnen und Absolventen sind ausdrücklich willkommen, ebenso Profile mit einigen Jahren Erfahrung.

  • Modernes Büro mit Terrasse, mitten im Münchner Werksviertel
